question: Who among the following headed the Constitutional States Committee formed for negotiating with the states?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawaharlal Nehru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was a key figure in the Indian independence movement and the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• He played a significant role in the drafting of the Indian Constitution and was a member of various committees including the Constitutional States Committee.
 
• The Constitutional States Committee was responsible for negotiating with the princely states regarding their integration into the Indian Union.
 
• Nehru's leadership and diplomatic skills were instrumental in ensuring the smooth integration of these states into the newly independent nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional States Committee:**

 
 
• The Constitutional States Committee was formed during the process of drafting the Indian Constitution to address the integration of princely states.
 
• Princely states were semi-autonomous regions ruled by local monarchs under the suzerainty of the British Crown.
 
• With India's independence, there was a need to integrate these states into the Indian Union to ensure political and administrative coherence.
 
• The committee was tasked with negotiating terms with the rulers of these states to facilitate their accession to India.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:**
 
 
• Nehru was a central figure in Indian politics both before and after independence.
 
• He was a close associate of Mahatma Gandhi and played a pivotal role in the Indian National Congress.
 
• As Prime Minister, Nehru laid the foundation for a modern, secular, and socialist India.
 
• His policies and vision continue to influence Indian politics and development.
 
 
 
• **Integration of Princely States:**
 
 
• Post-independence, India comprised British India and over 500 princely states.
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, the then Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Home Affairs, led the efforts for the political integration of these states.
 
• Most princely states acceded to India through the signing of the Instrument of Accession.
 
• This integration was crucial for the unity and stability of the newly independent nation.
